sample_unit: FAQ questions paired with ChatGPT responses

links.outcome: Readability grade levels of ChatGPT responses versus health organization FAQs on OUD
links.effect: ChatGPT grade levels were consistently higher: Coleman-Liau +3.43, Gunning Fog +3.47, SMOG +2.96, Flesch-Kincaid +3.61, ARI +4.33, Flesch Reading Ease -20.4 (all p < .05).
links.quote: Readability grade levels were consistently higher: Coleman-Liau +3.43, Gunning Fog +3.47, SMOG + 2.96, Flesch-Kincaid +3.61, Automated Readability Index +4.33, and Flesch Reading Ease -20.4 (all p < .05).

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated OUD patient education relative to FAQs
links.effect: ChatGPT responses were 3-4 grade levels higher across indices, longer (253.7 vs 76.6 words), with higher lexical density (+6.5 percentage points).
links.quote: ChatGPT produced more comprehensive but less readable content than FAQs, revealing a gap with health literacy standards.

unlisted_practices: Plain-language prompting of chatbots to reduce reading level
Screening AI patient education for stigmatizing language in OUD content

screen.reason: Evaluates readability, linguistic complexity, and stigma of ChatGPT (GPT-4o) responses to opioid use disorder FAQs compared to health organization FAQs, without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
